outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a read of the public data and news above, meant to help you decide, not a recommendation. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.reason: Nvidia and Broadcom are essentially flat to slightly up even as the broader chip complex sells off hard, as capital consolidates into the clearest AI-infrastructure names ahead of a heavy earnings slate (Microsoft and Meta tonight, Arm tonight, Amazon tomorrow).

Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Adobe are holding or extending recent sharp gains, with ServiceNow's AI annual contract value reportedly crossing $1 billion and CrowdStrike raising FY27 guidance — both reinforcing the theme that AI-monetizing software is outperforming AI-spending infrastructure names today.

weakest.reason: AMD, Arm, and Micron all fell sharply again as the AI-chip trade narrows to its clearest leaders, and ASML dropped on fresh reports of Chinese progress in immersion lithography reviving competitive-threat concerns.

weakest.area: Risk sentiment broadly, ahead of the Fed
weakest.reason: Alphabet, Palantir, and Ouster all pulled back, and crypto's fear-and-greed index sits at a subdued 35, reflecting a market that's cautious and event-driven rather than trending, with today's Fed decision the dominant variable.

outlook.nextStep: Today brings three major catalysts stacked together — the Fed's 2pm ET rate decision (Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair, with markets pricing ~68.5% odds of a hold), Microsoft and Meta earnings after the close, and Arm's earnings tonight — all worth watching closely rather than acting on ahead of time. Teradyne's clean 12.8% earnings pop is the more distinct, worth-a-closer-look signal today, since it's a concrete, dated data point on AI-related test-equipment demand rather than macro speculation.

signals.title: Fed decision today is Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair, with oil-driven inflation risk still lingering
signals.body: The FOMC concludes its two-day meeting today with a 2pm ET rate decision and 2:30pm press conference — the first meeting under new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh, who has offered few signals on his preferred communication style. CME FedWatch data puts the odds at roughly 68.5% for a hold at 3.50-3.75% (a fifth straight meeting unchanged) versus 31.5% for a hike, with the month's sharp oil-price rise keeping a headline-inflation scare alive.
signals.watch: The 2pm ET rate decision and, more importantly, the tone of the press conference for signals on how Warsh plans to communicate going forward.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a first meeting under new leadership with meaningful hike odds still priced in is a lot of event risk to sit in front of.

signals.title: AI-chip trade narrows sharply to Nvidia and Broadcom as second-tier names get cut hard
signals.body: AMD fell roughly 9% intraday, Arm dropped about 7% ahead of tonight's earnings, and Intel and Marvell also sold off, while Nvidia and Broadcom were roughly flat to slightly higher. Analysts describe this as investors consolidating exposure into the clearest AI-infrastructure leaders and trimming richly priced, higher-beta satellite names ahead of this week's heavy Big Tech earnings slate, rather than any single piece of negative company news.
signals.watch: Arm's earnings tonight and whether the leader/laggard gap narrows or widens further once Microsoft and Meta report.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a broad-based rotation within the same sector, rather than a single-stock story, tends to be more informative than an isolated move.

signals.title: ASML falls on fresh reports of Chinese progress in immersion lithography
signals.body: ASML shares dropped roughly 4% after reports that Chinese state-backed firms have advanced in producing immersion lithography equipment, reviving longstanding concerns about ASML's competitive moat amid U.S.-China tech tensions. Some analysts view the reaction as overdone given ASML's multi-year lead in extreme ultraviolet lithography specifically.
signals.watch: Any official ASML response or additional detail on the reported Chinese equipment's actual capability versus ASML's current technology.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — early-stage, second-hand reports about a competitor's progress are harder to verify than a dated, company-specific catalyst.

signals.title: Teradyne jumps 12.8% on a clean Q2 beat and raised guidance
signals.body: Teradyne reported Q2 revenue of $1.33 billion (nearly double last year's figure) and non-GAAP EPS of $2.47, well above the $2.09 consensus estimate, and raised Q3 guidance to $1.85-$2.15 EPS. Shares jumped in response, a notable positive data point for AI-related semiconductor test-equipment demand on a day when most of the chip complex sold off.
signals.watch: Whether other test-and-measurement or equipment names see similar demand commentary in upcoming earnings.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a concrete, better-than-expected earnings beat with raised guidance is one of the more dated and verifiable signals in today's update.

signals.title: Enterprise software and cybersecurity extend their rally, monetizing AI rather than spending on it
signals.body: Salesforce, ServiceNow, and Workday all surged in recent sessions and are holding those gains today, with ServiceNow's AI products reportedly crossing $1 billion in annual contract value and agentic deployments up ninefold in nine months. CrowdStrike separately raised its FY27 revenue guidance to $5.91-5.96 billion on AI-security demand. Palantir is a notable exception, pulling back roughly 5.6% even as peers rally.
signals.watch: Whether the rotation into AI-monetizing software holds through Microsoft and Meta's earnings tonight, and whether Palantir's divergence from the group persists or reverses.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — multiple companies posting similar AI-monetization data points on the same day looks like a real theme rather than one company's news.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum tick higher but sentiment stays cautious ahead of the Fed
signals.body: Bitcoin held above $63,000 (+1.0%) and Ethereum gained about 2.4%, but the crypto fear-and-greed index sits at a subdued 35, and multiple market commentators describe both assets as still under pressure and testing key technical levels heading into today's Fed decision.
signals.watch: How crypto reacts to the 2pm ET rate decision and press conference tone, given its recent tendency to trade in sympathy with broader risk assets.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — modest gains against a backdrop of subdued sentiment and a major pending catalyst make this a wait-and-see setup rather than a clear signal.

signals.title: Microsoft, Meta, and Arm all report earnings today — a pivotal moment for the AI trade
signals.body: Microsoft and Meta report after today's close, with Arm reporting the same evening, making this one of the most consequential single days of the earnings season for AI-infrastructure sentiment. Focus areas include Azure growth and AI-capex commentary for Microsoft, and how each company frames the return on heavy AI spending given the recent volatility in chip stocks.
signals.watch: Azure growth rate, any updated capex guidance, and Arm's own results given its rough month heading into tonight's print.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — three large, dated catalysts landing on the same day will likely set the tone for the AI trade into month-end.
